info.description: Unofficial. Reverse-engineered from the public Microsoft Learn documentation (learn.microsoft.com), then corrected and extended against recorded first-party traffic: operations and schemas carrying x-probe-verified were observed on the wire, everything else is docs-derived and unverified. Tags group operations by logical resource; x-ms-namespace records the namespace Microsoft files each under. Note the three servers: many operations are served only from the tenant- or environment-scoped host, whose name is derived from the tenant or environment id.

servers.description: Global endpoint. Every documented operation is reachable here; the gateway routes the request to the tenant's own cluster. First-party clients use it for operations that are not already scoped to one tenant or environment by the caller's context.

Tenant-scoped endpoint. The host is derived from the tenant id alone — there is no region or scale-unit in it. Remove the hyphens from the tenant id to get 32 hex characters, then split: the first 30 are the first DNS label and the remaining 2 are the second. Tenant `00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000ab` therefore resolves to `https://000000000000000000000000000000.ab.tenant.api.powerplatform.com`. Operations served only here act on the calling user or the tenant as a whole and take no tenant id in the path.

tenantIdHead.description: The first 30 characters of the tenant id with its hyphens removed.

tenantIdTail.description: The last 2 characters of the tenant id with its hyphens removed.

servers.description: Environment-scoped endpoint. Built from the environment id by the same rule as the tenant host: strip the hyphens to get 32 hex characters, take the first 30 as the first DNS label and the last 2 as the second. Environment `00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000ab` resolves to `https://000000000000000000000000000000.ab.environment.api.powerplatform.com`. The environment is implied by the host, so these paths carry no `/environments/{environmentId}` segment — `/connectivity/connections` here is the same resource as `/connectivity/environments/{environmentId}/connections` on the global host.

environmentIdHead.description: The first 30 characters of the environment id with its hyphens removed.

environmentIdTail.description: The last 2 characters of the environment id with its hyphens removed.

securityScheme.description: Microsoft Entra ID OAuth2. The audience is `https://api.powerplatform.com` for all three hosts — the tenant- and environment-scoped hosts take the same token as the global one, so there is nothing per-host to acquire. Requesting `.default` yields whatever delegated permissions the client application has been granted; `x-delegated-scopes` lists the granular permissions observed in real first-party tokens. Which scope each operation actually requires was not established — the tokens show what was granted, not what was needed.

Cluster.description: The regional service cluster that serves a tenant or an environment. Its name appears in the `x-ms-gateway-clusters` response header on every call and identifies which stamp, geography and release ring the caller is talking to.

Copilot Governance Setting.description: A single tenant- or environment-level consent switch for a generative AI capability — typically whether a named model provider may be used as a subprocessor. Each setting carries its own admin-centre presentation, the rule that backs it and the effective value.

Feature Gate.description: A named feature flag as evaluated for the caller or the environment. Read-only: the platform decides the value and reports where it came from.

Governance Configuration.description: Tenant-authored governance content surfaced to makers in the maker portal, addressed by configuration name.

Notification.description: In-product notifications for the calling maker, and the Web PubSub channel that pushes them live.

Service Plan.description: The Power Platform service plans (licences) assigned to the calling user, and the policy limits each plan grants.

User Setting.description: A per-user preference blob stored against the caller's Entra object id and addressed by setting name. The maker portal uses them to persist UI state; each setting name has its own free-form shape.

POST /powerapps/apps/{appName}/startSess.description: Opens an editing session on the app and returns every session currently open on it. The studio calls this when an app is opened for edit; the response is what drives co-presence and the warning that someone else already holds the writer session. Sessions expire ten minutes after their last update, so a client that means to keep the app open must call this again.

EnvironmentManagementSetting.description: One environment's management settings, one property per setting. Every property name is PascalCase on the wire — `Id`, `PowerApps_AllowCodeApps` — and `$select` matches it case-sensitively. The docs render each name with a lowercased leading letter; the names below are the wire spelling where recorded traffic established it. A setting that has never been set is returned as an explicit `null`.

Id.description: The environment id. Always returned, whatever `$select` asks for.

PowerApps_AllowCodeApps.description: Whether makers may run code apps — apps authored outside Power Apps and brought in to run on the platform. Turning it off stops existing code apps running. `null` until the setting has ever been set.

PowerApps_EnableGenerativePages.description: Whether generative pages may be created in this environment. Not in the docs; observed on the wire and accepted by `$select`.

CopilotStudio_ComputerUseEnabled.description: Whether Copilot Studio agents may use computer use — driving another system's graphical interface with a vision model. Named as a rule input by the rule-set UI configuration; absent from the docs.

CopilotStudio_ComputerUseDedicatedMachin.description: Whether computer use may run on machines dedicated to this tenant. Named as a rule input by the rule-set UI configuration; absent from the docs.

CopilotStudio_ComputerUseByoMachines.description: Whether computer use may run on machines the customer brings. Named as a rule input by the rule-set UI configuration; absent from the docs.

CopilotStudio_ExternalModels.description: Whether makers may build on non-Microsoft models in Copilot Studio. Backs the per-provider consent switches under [Copilot Governance Setting](#/operations/copilotgovernance_getSetting); absent from the docs.

BapLifecycleOperation.description: A Business Application Platform lifecycle operation, returned when polling the Location handed back by an async environment-group membership change. Not documented; shape verified against the live API.

id.description: Lifecycle status. NotStarted, Succeeded and Failed were verified against the live API; the API also returns in-progress states that were not observed, so treat the set as open.
Lifecycle status. NotStarted, Succeeded and Failed were verified against the live API; the API also returns in-progress states that were not observed, so treat the set as open.

RbacRoleAssignment.description: A role assignment as returned by the authorization endpoints. Shape verified against the live API; the documentation models the item as a role definition instead.

RbacRoleAssignmentList.description: An OData collection of role assignments. Verified against the live API.

PowerAppsUserSetting.description: One named preference blob for the calling user. The resource id is scoped to the caller's Entra object id, so the same setting name reads back differently for different users.

name.description: The setting name as the service stores it. The path segment is matched case-insensitively but the stored name is echoed back with its own casing, so a request for `paOrgApps` answers with `PAOrgApps`.

settings.description: The stored preference, free-form and specific to the setting name. Recorded examples: `powerApps_makerSettings` holds `language`, `dateFormat`, `timeFormat`, `country` and `optIn`; `modernLeftNavToolbox_prod` holds a `value` array of pinned navigation item ids; `userProfile` holds visit counters; dismissible teaching callouts such as `frx` and `PAOrgApps` hold `dismissed` and `finished` booleans; `preferredsolutioncard_prod` holds `isVisible`.

PowerAppsFeature.description: One feature gate as evaluated for the caller or the environment.

id.description: Resource id. Tenant-scoped reads return `/providers/Microsoft.PowerApps/objectIds/{objectId}/features/{name}`; environment-scoped reads return `/providers/Microsoft.PowerApps/features/{name}`.

featureDescription.description: What the gate controls, in Microsoft's own words.

settingSource.description: Where the value came from. `FeatureGate` means an explicit flight or override applies; `NotSpecified` means the platform default is in force.

PowerAppsFeatureList.description: Every feature gate that currently evaluates to enabled for the requested scope. Gates that are off are omitted rather than returned as false, so absence is the negative answer. Recorded responses ran to 765 entries; there is no paging envelope.

PowerAppsEnvironmentPermission.description: One operation the caller may perform on the environment.

PowerAppsEnvironmentProperties.description: Environment properties as the maker portal sees them. This is the Business Application Platform environment record, not the environmentmanagement projection: it uses `azureRegionHint`/`azureRegion` rather than `location`, and nests lifecycle state under `states`.

azureRegionHint.description: The Azure region the environment was asked for.

azureRegion.description: The Azure region the environment actually runs in.

creationType.description: How the environment came to exist.

isDefault.description: Whether this is the tenant's default environment.

databaseType.description: Present only once Dataverse is provisioned.

retentionPeriod.description: Backup retention as an ISO 8601 duration.

lifecycleAuthority.description: Which system owns lifecycle operations on the environment.

enableAnalyticsForMakers.description: Whether makers may see analytics for their own apps.

protectionLevel.description: `Basic` means the environment is not managed; `Standard` means Managed Environment governance applies.

parentEnvironmentGroup.description: The environment group the environment belongs to. The all-zeros GUID is the sentinel for 'no group' — the field is present even when the environment is ungrouped.

id.description: Environment group id, or the all-zeros GUID when ungrouped.

runtime.description: Runtime state — this is where an admin-disabled environment shows up.

cluster.description: The stamp serving this environment. `uriSuffix` is the host fragment that appears in per-environment runtime endpoints such as the Copilot Studio one.

clientUris.description: Deep links into the first-party portals for this environment.

runtimeEndpoints.description: Per-service regional base URLs, keyed by service name (`microsoft.BusinessAppPlatform`, `microsoft.PowerApps`, `microsoft.Flow`, `microsoft.CommonDataModel`, `microsoft.PowerVirtualAgents`, `microsoft.ApiManagement`, `microsoft.PowerAppsAdvisor`). A client that hardcodes a global host instead of reading these will talk to the wrong geography.

linkedEnvironmentMetadata.description: The Dataverse organization backing this environment, when there is one.

baseLanguage.description: LCID of the organization's base language.

connectedGroups.description: Populated only when `$expand` asks for it.

permissions.description: What the caller may do here, keyed by permission name (`CreatePowerApp`, `ReadEnvironment`, `DeleteEnvironment`, `SetDLPPolicy`, …). Returned only when the request asks for `$expand=properties.permissions`; a permission the caller lacks is absent rather than false.

PowerAppsEnvironmentResource.description: An environment as the maker-facing Power Apps surface returns it.

name.description: The environment id. For a tenant's default environment this is `Default-{tenantId}` rather than a bare GUID, so it is not always parseable as a UUID.

nextLink.description: Present only when more environments remain.

ServicePlanPolicies.description: What the plan lets its holder do. Limits of `0` generally mean 'none granted by this plan' rather than 'unlimited'; entitlement is the union across the caller's plans.

accessPremiumApis.description: Whether premium connectors may be used.

accessOnPremGateway.description: Whether on-premises data gateways may be used.

accessAdminRoutes.description: Whether the holder may call admin endpoints.

canUseCustomApis.description: Whether custom connectors may be *used*; `customApiLimit` caps how many may be created.

calendarMonthFlowRunLimit.description: Cloud flow runs per calendar month.

maximumRecurrenceFrequency.description: Fastest recurrence trigger the plan permits.

flowPlanEnforcementScope.description: Whether flow limits are counted per user or per tenant.

onlyAllowAppUsage.description: A run-only plan: the holder may play apps but not author them.

powerAppsTeamsOnly.description: The plan is the Power Apps for Teams entitlement.

rpaAttendedAllowed.description: Whether attended desktop flows may run.

pcfExternalServiceUsageAllowed.description: Whether PCF code components may call external services.

ServicePlan.description: One service plan assigned to the calling user.

properties.description: The plan and what it grants.

correlationGroup.description: Groups plans that are variants of the same product, so a client can collapse them in a licence summary.

licensePriority.description: Ordering hint — the lowest number wins when the platform picks one plan to attribute usage to.

isGuestPlan.description: Whether the plan comes from a tenant the caller is a guest in.

MakerEnrollment.description: The calling user's first-run state in this tenant: which tenant they landed in, which environment is the default, and what they are licensed for.

isTenantWhitelisted.description: Whether the tenant may use Power Apps at all.

isGccTenant.description: Whether the tenant is in a US Government cloud.

defaultEnvironmentName.description: Name of the tenant's default environment, of the form `Default-{tenantId}`.

backfillEnvironmentName.description: Environment the platform will place resources in when the caller has not chosen one. Normally the same as `defaultEnvironmentName`.

aadTenantLocation.description: Geography Entra ID reports for the tenant. A mismatch with `defaultLocation` means the default environment sits outside the directory's home geography.

items.description: Directory facts mirrored from Microsoft Graph.

enrollmentOptions.description: Choices the caller has already made during onboarding.

NotificationChannelSubscription.description: A short-lived Azure Web PubSub client credential. Connect the returned URL as a WebSocket to receive notifications live; re-subscribe before `expirationTime` to stay connected.

url.description: WebSocket URL with the access token already embedded in the query string. Treat it as a secret — it authenticates the bearer.

expirationTime.description: When the embedded token stops working. Recorded lifetime was roughly 12 hours.

clusterNumber.description: Stamp number within the geography. Zero-padded, and a string, not a number.

clusterType.description: `CustomerManagement` serves the tenant-scoped host; `IslandCluster` serves the environment-scoped host.

clusterCategory.description: Release ring. `FirstRelease` stamps take service updates ahead of `Prod`.

environment.description: Service environment the stamp belongs to.

geoLongName.description: Geography name as used in runtime endpoint hostnames.

inputName.description: Rule input name, matching a property in the environment's management settings.

settingName.description: The governance setting the input sets.

isLegacyRule.description: True for settings still carried by the pre-rule-set governance model.

CopilotGovernanceSetting.description: A single generative AI consent switch, with its effective value and everything the admin centre needs to render it.

resourceId.description: Where the value is stored, of the form `copilotgovernance/tenants/{tenantId}/environments/{environmentId}/settings/{settingName}`.

value.description: The effective value for this environment.

defaultValue.description: What applies when nothing has been set. Note this can be `true` while `value` is `false`, and while `isDisabled` is `true`.

checkboxLabel.description: Label for the toggle in the admin centre; present only for settings that render as a checkbox.

settingState.description: Release stage of the capability the setting governs.

isManagedEnvironmentProperty.description: Whether changing it requires a Managed Environment.

invertValue.description: When true the stored value is the negation of what the admin centre shows — the switch reads as 'block' rather than 'allow'.

enabledStatus.description: How widely the capability is switched on above this environment.

RuleSetUiComponent.description: One control in the rule set's editor.

componentId.description: Ordinal within the rule set, as a string.

text.description: Label shown next to the control. May contain literal `\n` escapes that the client is expected to render as line breaks.

RuleSetUiConfiguration.description: The presentation contract for one rule set: which settings it writes, how the admin centre renders them, and which feature gate has to be on for it to appear at all. Reading it is the only way to discover a rule set's input names without guessing.

featureFlag.description: Gate controlling whether this rule set is offered.

name.description: Title shown in the admin centre.

isPreview.description: Whether the capability is still in preview.

enableConfigBasedRuleRender.description: Whether the client should render from this configuration rather than from its own built-in layout for the rule set.

RuleSetUiConfigurationList.description: Every rule set the tenant may configure.

AppDlpEvaluationRequest.description: The app to evaluate, sent as the app document rather than by id — the point is to evaluate a draft before it is saved. Only the connector-bearing parts matter: `databaseReferences` and the app's connection references drive the verdict. Which fields are genuinely required was not established: every recorded call sent the whole document.

tags.description: The app's tag bag, as it would be saved.

properties.description: The app document. Recorded requests carried `appUris`, `environment` (`id` and `name`), `displayName`, `description`, `commitMessage`, `backgroundColor`, `minClientVersion`, `createdByClientVersion`, `lifeCycleId`, `enableModernRuntimeMode`, `appCopilotReference` and `databaseReferences`.

databaseReferences.description: Dataverse references keyed by database name (`default.cds`), each with `databaseDetails` and `dataSources`.

violations.description: One entry per breached rule. Empty in every recorded response, so the item shape is not established here.

violationsByPolicy.description: The same violations grouped by the policy that raised them.

violationErrorMessage.description: Prose summary. Present and populated even when the app is compliant — it lists the connectors that were considered, and is `"The app uses the following connectors: ."` for an app with none. Do not read it as an error.

AppDlpEvaluationResponse.description: Result of evaluating an unsaved app against the environment's data loss prevention policies.

errors.description: Evaluation failures, as distinct from policy violations. Empty in every recorded response.

AppSession.description: One editing session on the app.

userClientContext.description: Opaque client context, echoed back verbatim. The studio puts a JSON string here carrying its own `clientSessionId`.

expiry.description: When the session lapses if not renewed. Recorded lifetime was 10 minutes from `lastUpdatedTime`.

AppSessionRequest.description: Which kind of session to open. Both fields were sent on every recorded call; neither was proved required.

sessionType.description: `Writer` claims the edit lock; `Reader` joins without claiming it.

userClientContext.description: Opaque string echoed back on every session in the response, so a client can recognise its own tabs.

AppSessionResponse.description: The caller's new session, plus every other session currently open on the app — this is what drives the co-authoring presence indicator and the 'someone else is editing' warning.

sessions.description: Open sessions keyed by session id, the caller's own included.

AppLocation.description: Where an app lives. Answering this is the whole point of the operation: given only an app id, it returns the tenant, environment and geography needed to build the environment-scoped host for every subsequent call.

geo.description: Geography short name, matching `geoLongName` on the gateway cluster.

isGlobalApp.description: Whether the app is one of the Microsoft-published sample apps rather than a tenant's own.
